I can prepare e PR with proposed solution.

## Description

Each CMS `Page` can have one `PageUrl` object per language. If there are more than that, a `MultipleObjectsReturned`-exception may be raised.


## Steps to reproduce

* Edit the page which is set as Home.
* Save the content.
* Publish that page.

The `PageUrl`-object for the home page now has two entries in the database. Reason is this 
https://github.com/django-cms/django-cms/blob/21d6a6defc5a6321bd691e43eb57c112508b952f/cms/models/pagemodel.py#L292-L296
code snippet. Here `new_path` is a functional expression containing `Concat(ConcatPair(Value('parent_slug'), ConcatPair(Value('/'), F(slug))))`. Since the resulting `path` field of the home page must be an empty string the above query can't work.

## Alternative reproduction

* Create a page with a named slug and publish as a subpage of another page. 
* Create another page with the same slug, but as child of another parent page.
* Move one of those pages so that they become siblings.

Now we get two objects of `PageUrl` with the same `language` and the same `path` entry for different pages. This in my opinion is inconsistent.

I therefore strongly recommend to add `unique_together = [['path', 'language'], ['page', 'language']]` to the `Meta`-class of the `PageUrl`-class.

In my setup I already did this. This is how I found out about the two errors reported before. Otherwise I rarely ran into the problem of hitting a `MultipleObjectsReturned`-exception, whose real cause then of course is much harder to detect.

There are a lot of deprecation warnings when running on django 1.10, which django CMS supports. It would probably be a good idea to clean those up. 

### Expected behaviour

no deprecation warnings

### Actual behaviour

Lots of warnings. Note: since django 1.10, you have to run python with `-Wd` to see the warnings. Might be a good idea to do that when running the tests suite.

Here's a list of all the warnings:

1. "Importing from `django.core.urlresolvers` is deprecated in favor of `django.urls`".
    - This is done in several places.
2. "on_delete will be a required arg for `OneToOneField` in Django 2.0. Set it to `models.CASCADE` on models and in existing migrations if you want to maintain the current default behavior." 
    - This warning happens all over the place. 
    - To fix, every `ForeignKey` in all existing migrations need to set `on_delete=models.CASCADE` if they do not already specify `on_delete`. Then, set `on_delete=models.CASCADE` on all `ForeignKey`'s in all models, unless cascade is not the intended behavior. If the behavior should be different, new migrations will need to be created after changing  the models.

As a result, the 'objects' manager won't be created (or recreated) automatically anymore on 'cms.PageUserGroup' and 'objects' declared on 'auth.Group' will be promoted to default manager. Hi everyone, sorry for not using a template but this is not for a bug template.

I have a technical question regarding performance optimizations for CMS. I’ve noticed that retrieving titles of the pages are not optimized and I’m wondering is there a reason why it was implemented like this. Here is an example:

`[page.get_title() for page in Page.objects.filter(id__in=[1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7])]`

Creates 8 queries to the database, but if you add a prefetch_related to the query set it also does 8+1 queries (one is for retrieving all the titles for these pages):

`[page.get_title() for page in Page.objects.prefetch_related("title_set").filter(id__in=[1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7])]`

This can be optimized if we change the way the title cache is populated on the line:
https://github.com/django-cms/django-cms/blob/develop/cms/models/pagemodel.py#L1434.

Instead of doing
`titles = Title.objects.filter(page=self)`
we could do
`titles = self.title_set.all()`

And this will create only two queries, and the number of queries won’t increase linearly with the number of pages.
I’m wondering is there a reason why titles are fetched this way?

I could create a PR if DjangoCMS core contributors agree on the change.
title: Potential performance optimization for fetching Page titles

Sometimes a plugin can cause an exception based on whatever is entered by the user, or because of other causes (e.g an api that is unreachable). Obviously this is a bug in the plugin, but it can happen and it can happen on production servers. Currently we let the exception bubble up and show a 500 page. In production this is a desaster, because with frontend editing, you can't even navigate the the page and remove the offending plugin anymore. The user is completely blocked concerning that page and has to get a developer to fix the bug before any more content can be entered on the page.

I propose that plugin rendering for each plugin has a try/except around it. To Visitors the offending plugin should just not be rendered (or an error message?). To content editors the plugin should be rendered in a way that is clear that something went wrong (perhaps with a red border and a message in the notification area at the top of the screen). In structure view the plugin should also be highlighted. In any case it should be possible to still edit or remove the plugin.
In any case the error should be logged with a traceback.

This behaviour should be controlled by a new setting that uses `DEBUG` as a default but can be overridden.
title: graceful plugin exceptions

Find "on page level" (fields description) > "View restricted" (checkbox label). ### "frontend view restriction" 1. Go to '`/admin/cms/globalpagepermissions/add`. 2. Find "on page level" (fields description) > "View restricted" (checkbox label). 3. Underneath it, read "frontend view restriction". ### "Edit permissions required" 1. Go to '`/admin/cms/globalpagepermissions/add`. 2. Add permission for user or group: 1. Check "Can publish". 2. Check nothing else. 4. Submit 5. See error "Users can't […] Edit permissions required." ## Expected behaviour Text that has less interpretations, and such that the correct interpretation is easy to determine. ### "View restricted" Because it actually means `not can_view` ([ref.](https://django-cmsworkspace.slack.com/archives/C01EBCEK49E/p1692688566786649?thread_ts=1692654745.963519&cid=C01EBCEK49E)), maybe something like: > Can not view restricted pages. But, what are "restricted pages"? ### "frontend view restriction" Because it actually describes `not can_view` ([ref.](https://django-cmsworkspace.slack.com/archives/C01EBCEK49E/p1692688566786649?thread_ts=1692654745.963519&cid=C01EBCEK49E)), mayeb soemthing like: > Hides restricted pages from selected user/group. But, what are "restricted pages"? But how to keep "Can edit" in sync with the label text to which it refers? ### "[…] Edit permissions required" Maybe, > Ensure user has "Can edit" permission But how to keep "Can edit" in sync with the label text to which it refers? ## Actual behaviour ### "View restricted" Label text "View restricted" is unclear because of multiple interpretations: - "View (as a verb) restricted [what]". - "View [of … what … is] restricted". ### "frontend view restriction" Help text "frontend view restriction" is unclear because of it creates more questions than it answers: - There is a restriction? - This makes a restriction? - Is the restriction active when checked or not checked? - Can I restrict a backend view from this page? ### "[…] Edit permissions required" Error text "Edit permissions required" is unclear because of multiple interpretations: - "Edit permissions [are] required." - "Edit (as a verb) [the] permissions [that are] required." ## Screenshots | View restricted | frontend view restriction | […] Edit permissions required | | - | - | - | | ![View restricted](https://github.com/django-cms/django-cms/assets/62723358/4aff7269-df28-451f-a8bf-45a1354b41f7) | ![frontend view restriction](https://github.com/django-cms/django-cms/assets/62723358/ad7c3ea7-b779-4ab9-a7f8-4bd970bf94ef) | | ## Additional information (CMS/Python/Django versions) - Django CMS: 3.8.0 - Django: 3.2 - Python: 1.4.0 ## Do you want to help fix this issue? * Yes, I want to help fix this issue and I will join #workgroup-pr-review on [Slack](https://www.django-cms.org/slack) to confirm with the community that a PR is welcome. * Maybe, and if Yes, then I agree to the above. * [x] No, I only want to report the issue. ## Description Django CMS 4 lacks ## Steps to reproduce For this to observe, `CMS_PERMISSION = True` needs to be set in `settings.py`. ## Description

If a page title contains special characters, such as `&`, then this character is rendered as HTML-entity, for instance `&`.
In browser tabs this does not look right.


## Steps to reproduce

* Create a page template where the page title is used. This usually is done by adding

```html
…
<meta>
  {% page_attribute "page_title" as page_title %}
  <title>{{ page_title}}</title>
  …
</meta>
…
```


* Create or edit a page and use `A & B` as the page title.
* Load the page.

The browser tab shows `A & B`.

## Expected behaviour

The browser tab should show `A & B` as page title.


## Do you want to help fix this issue?

By patching the templatetag `cms.templatetags.cms_tags.PageAttribute` and [not escaping the value](https://github.com/django-cms/django-cms/blob/fa7b89ceec3bd22e031be8e9cf2328a3f9434b12/cms/templatetags/cms_tags.py#L411), this can be fixed easily. However, I don't know what security implications this fix may have.

I would exempt escaping the string, whenever the name is `page_title`, just as we do it with values of type `datetime`.

Any objections to this?

* [ ] No, I only want to report the issue.

## Description

When adding a plugin or editing a plugin the so-called "data bridge" updates the frontend editor of django CMS by providing changes in the plugin tree. To the frontend, three "types" of plugins are important: 
* Regular plugins (corresponding to a `CMSPlugin`model object)
* Placeholders (which is where the regular plugins live)
* General plugins (which connect some part of a template to a Django model object. Double-clicking it opens a modal to edit the object) - see https://docs.django-cms.org/en/latest/how_to/06-frontend_models.html

The data bridge updates the first two items but does not update these "general plugins". 

If you add or edit a plugin that shows a frontend-editable Django model, it will not be editable before reloading the page. This interrupts the workflow of editors.

## Description

Django async support adapts synchronous middleware to an asynchronous middleware stack automagically.  It does that by assuming it's synchronous and testing for async.  Subclassing MiddlewareMixin makes that test positive.  However, some cms middleware then overrides \_\_call\_\_, which django does not adapt, causing it to fail.

Of the five middlewares provided, LanguageCookieMiddleware and CurrentUserMiddleware both suffer from this.

## Steps to reproduce

Run django-cms on an ASGI server (uvicorn in my case).

## Expected behaviour

Django async support allows non-async django-cms to run alongside async-aware apps.

## Actual behaviour

Failure is immediate if LanguageCookieMiddleware is installed:

The menu cache works by creating a unique cache key for each user, site & language combo.
If the user is not logged in, then the key is unique for site and language only.

Because these keys are created for each user, the cms stores a reference to the keys in the database under the model `CacheKey`, this allows the cms to delete all cached entries when something changes, without having to recompute the key for every user.

When a page is requested, the cms will load the menu which as a first step checks if the cache key for this user exists in the cache server, if it does then it will immediately return the result, otherwise it will discover and process all menu nodes and then store the nodes in the cache server **and** create a reference to the key used on the cache server, in the `CacheKey` model.

This pattern can lead to a case where if the cache key does not exist in the database (`CacheKey` model) but it exists in the cache server, any content that is there will be served, even though it could be outdated.

Normally, when a page is published or changed, the cms will clear the cache.
Clearing the cache involves getting all keys from the `CacheKey` model and deleting each one through django's cache api.

But there is a problem where the keys go out of sync, thus recreating the scenario mentioned above.

This problem was introduced by https://github.com/divio/django-cms/pull/1252, where cache keys in the database are cleared but their counterpart in the cache server are not.

To reproduce this, depending on the machine used, make two requests at the same time and make a third one exactly one second after the first two.
title: Menu cache keys are not expiring correctly

### Summary

I have a site where I don't need international URLs, so I disabled them by not using `i18n_patterns` in `urls.py`.

Let's say I have two cms pages:

* Home (path / without language prefix)
* Foo (path /foo and also without language prefix)

In the advanced settings of Foo, I can select the entry "Home (/)" in the redirect field. After submitting the form, I get the following error: "Enter a valid URL."

The redirect field (`PageSmartLinkField`) uses `validate_url`. `validate_url` gets `value='/'` and calls `RegexValidator(regex=relative_url_regex)(value)`. I think the issue is that `relative_url_regex` does not match the path `/`. It only matches paths like e.g. `/foo`.

I suggest to modify `relative_url_regex` so that it also matches `/` and `./` since these are valid paths.

Redirect field accepts `/`.

#### Actual behaviour

* Django version: 1.10.7
